title: DataStoreService
summary: Persistent cloud storage: GetDataStore gives you key → value stores that survive server shutdowns. GetAsync reads, SetAsync overwrites, UpdateAsync modifies atomically. Budget-limited and throttle-prone — always pcall + retry.

verification.notes: Budget/throttle numbers change over time; keep to general guidance rather than exact quotas.

methods.name: GetDataStore
methods.description: Opens (or creates) a named store. Same name + same game = same store, forever.

methods.name: GetOrderedDataStore
methods.description: Store whose numeric values can be ranked (GetSortedAsync) — classic leaderboards.

details.heading: DataStore members
details.body: `GetAsync(key)` → current value (nil if none). `SetAsync(key, value)` → overwrite. `UpdateAsync(key, transformFn)` → atomic read-modify-write; the transform receives the old value and returns the new one (return nil to cancel). `RemoveAsync(key)`. `IncrementAsync(key, delta)` for counters.

details.heading: Value restrictions
details.body: Values must be serializable: tables of primitives, strings, numbers, booleans (no Instances, functions, or NaN/±inf). Size cap around 4 MB per value; strings recommended under 64KB for performance.

details.heading: Budgets and throttling
details.body: Requests consume a budget scaled with player count. Exceeding it throws throttling errors — hence pcall + retry with backoff, batching saves, and saving on PlayerRemoving + periodically.

details.heading: Studio access
details.body: Studio needs 'Enable Studio Access to API Services' (Game Settings → Security) to touch production stores; otherwise Studio uses a separate sandbox.

explanation.whatItIs: The game's long-term memory. Coins, levels, inventory — anything that must survive leaving the game lives in a DataStore keyed per player.
explanation.whyItExists: Server memory dies with the server. DataStores are Roblox's managed, replicated, durable key-value cloud built into the platform.
whenToUse: Player profiles: `key = "Player_" .. userId`, value = save table
Global data: server MOTD, seasonal state (a shared key)
whenNotToUse: High-frequency writes — budgets will throttle you; batch and debounce
Storing huge blobs or non-serializable values
As a message bus between servers — use MessagingService for pub/sub
Trusting Studio sandbox data as production data
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
GetDataStore("PlayerData")
        │
        ├─ GetAsync("Player_123")      → saved table or nil
        ├─ UpdateAsync("Player_123", fn) → atomic modify
        └─ SetAsync("Player_123", data)  → overwrite

Rules of survival:
  pcall everything · retry with backoff · save on leave
  save periodically · never trust one write
```
tips: Wrap every call in pcall + retry — network and throttling failures are normal
UpdateAsync for anything concurrent (trading, shared counters) — it's atomic
Version your save schema (`data.version = 2`) so you can migrate later
Save on PlayerRemoving AND on a periodic loop (crash insurance); BindToClose for shutdown saves
commonMistakes: No pcall: one throttle error kills the saving script
Saving every second per player — instant budget exhaustion; debounce/batch
SetAsync races: two writes clobbering each other — use UpdateAsync
Forgetting BindToClose — servers shutting down lose the last save
Testing against production data in Studio without realizing Studio Access is on

examples.title: The complete, safe player-data pattern
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData_v1")
local cache = {}   -- userId → data

local function withRetry(fn, attempts)
    for i = 1, attempts do
        local ok, result = pcall(fn)
        if ok then return result end
        warn(`Attempt {i}: {result}`)
        task.wait(1)
    end
    return nil
end

local function loadData(player)
    local key = "Player_" .. player.UserId
    local data = withRetry(function()
        return store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
            return old or { coins = 0, level = 1, version = 1 }
        end)
    end, 3)
    cache[player.UserId] = data or { coins = 0, level = 1, version = 1 }
end

local function saveData(player)
    local data = cache[player.UserId]
    if not data then return end
    withRetry(function()
        store:SetAsync("Player_" .. player.UserId, data)
    end, 3)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(loadData)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(saveData)

-- Periodic safety save every 5 minutes
while true do
    task.wait(300)
    for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
        task.spawn(saveData, player)
    end
end
examples.whyItWorks: UpdateAsync creates the default atomically if missing; retries absorb throttling; saving on leave plus periodically covers crashes and disconnects.
